newsitem.title: CANADA: Scott's, PepsiCo Canada delay trial.
newsitem.headline: Scott's, PepsiCo Canada delay trial.

text.p: Scott's Restaurants Inc and Pepsi-Cola Canada Ltd, a unit of PepsiCo Inc, said on Wednesday they delayed the opening of their trial over outstanding litigation to February 10, 1997, from November 18.
Scott's Restaurants was created to bypass a lawsuit by Pepsi-Cola Canada which had stalled Laidlaw Inc's takeover of Scott's Hospitality Inc.

Waste management and transportation giant Laidlaw had originally proposed to acquire Scott's Hospitality, keep the transport unit and sell the fast food division to privately held A&W Food Services of Canada Inc. But Pepsi-Cola Canada, which provides support to the Kentucky Fried Chicken (KFC) outlets, and Scott's Hospitality became embroiled in a legal dispute over the sale. Scott's spun off its units and Laidlaw bought the transport unit in July.

The litigation includes three claims by Pepsi-Cola Canada. Pepsi-Cola claimed that Scott's Food Services Inc (SFSI) "failed to comply with its contractual obligations to remodel and upgrade its KFC outlets."

It claimed "it has a contractual right to approve a sale of shares in SFSI or its parent company, that Pepsi has a right of first refusal on such a sale of shares, and that the recent reorganization of SFSI into the new parent company Scott's Restaurants Inc. breached these contractual rights."
Pepsi-Cola also claimed it has a right to damages and can end SFSI's franchise agreement because of the above breaches.
